articles: srcset-responsive-covers
Deliver responsive game art with accurate srcset and sizes
Images
A card that occupies 300 CSS pixels on a phone need not download a 1600-pixel marketing illustration; choose candidates based on displayed slot width and pixel density.

Produce and label several real width variants, provide a sizes expression matching CSS and retain an ordinary src fallback with alt. Inspect the browser currentSrc property instead of assuming it selects the smallest file.
For a card displayed 300 pixels wide at DPR 2, a 640-pixel candidate is a reasonable starting point. A 960-pixel candidate may be useful on wider displays.
An inaccurate sizes attribute can choose oversized files. Compare network bytes on 360-pixel and 1440-pixel viewports at multiple DPR settings.
IMG,LCP
art-directed-mobile-crops
Make mobile game banners readable without losing the subject
Images
A wide desktop hero may hide its main character behind a narrow viewport crop. Shrinking and cropping are different design choices, not interchangeable responsive techniques.
Use a picture element for art direction, offer deliberate portrait and landscape focal crops and check titles against visual subjects at every breakpoint.
A character placed on the far-right edge of a 16:9 source may need a different portrait crop with central framing, rather than object-position center alone.
Do not create mobile art from an older build and desktop art from a new one. Track both assets under a shared release ID and compare screenshots.
IMG,WCAG
verify-webp-signatures
Verify browser-produced WebP files using the container signature
Images
A Canvas export request for WebP can silently fall back to another format depending on browser capability, leaving files mislabeled by an extension alone.
Check the Blob type and confirm RIFF bytes at offsets zero through three and WEBP at offsets eight through eleven. Decode the output and inspect transparency and dimensions.
A valid RIFF/WEBP prefix is useful for format classification, but it cannot by itself prove the entire file is safe or complete.
Reject unsupported fallback outputs instead of presenting a PNG as WebP. Test malformed files, JPEG source input and transparent PNG source input.
IMG,UPLOAD
codec-visual-comparison
Compare AVIF, WebP and PNG based on perceptual quality
Images
Compression ratio is only useful if the game logo, thin UI text and illustration gradients survive at acceptable quality.
Export the same crop using a controlled encoder and several quality settings, evaluate at 100% and 200% view and measure decoded performance on a low-end mobile device.
A 55 KB file with unreadable white lettering is less useful than a 75 KB file whose character and label remain sharp; inspect important semantic details.
Comparing different crop dimensions can misattribute savings to a codec. Keep dimensions identical and include browser support in the release decision.
IMG,CWV
alt-text-game-catalog
Write meaningful alternative text for game cover links
Images
A card image named cover-final-9.webp supplies no helpful context when read aloud. Users need the image purpose rather than the asset filename.
Describe the relevant game scene and avoid repeating the entire link label. Empty alt is appropriate for decoration that adds nothing beyond adjacent text.
For a puzzle cover already linked as Prism Relay, alt could describe a gold beam crossing a blue grid of angled mirrors, giving a usable visual cue.
Keywords stuffed into alt harm clarity. Test a screen reader reading one gallery card at a time, including only the image link context.
WCAG,IMG
private-photo-metadata
Reduce unintended disclosure when exporting customer-supplied photos
Images
Camera originals can carry EXIF metadata that has no reason to accompany a game community showcase or product sample.
Decode, resize and re-encode to a controlled image type; inspect the resulting metadata rather than assuming all converters strip location fields. Limit retention of originals.
A visible street sign or address embedded in pixels remains sensitive even when metadata chunks are gone; use a human visual review for such cases.
Re-encoding can expose parser attacks if untrusted inputs are not bounded. Test oversized dimensions, malformed headers and output metadata.
UPLOAD,IMG
intrinsic-size-contract
Reserve space before images finish loading
Images
Product pages can shift repeatedly if newly decoded cover art pushes descriptive text and pricing controls downward.
Set intrinsic width and height and retain aspect-ratio-aware CSS. For art-directed picture sources, confirm the intended ratio in each alternate layout.
A 400×240 cover sets a 5:3 slot; a portrait replacement should declare its true dimensions rather than borrow those of the desktop source.
Using object-fit without a reserved slot does not itself stop layout shift. Test slow-network render and text scaling in a 390-pixel viewport.
CLS,IMG
sprite-atlas-tradeoffs
Choose sprite atlases using memory and draw-call evidence
Images
Hundreds of sprites as separate assets add request overhead, but one oversized atlas can consume GPU memory even for unseen animations.
Group atlases by scene lifetime and measure both transfer bytes and decoded RGBA area. Include padding around sprite borders and test fractional scaling.
A 1024×1024 RGBA atlas requires roughly four megabytes before mipmaps; two unused atlases held in memory may cost more than separate small files.
Aggressive packing can cause texture bleeding at small scales. Test art sharpness, resident memory and batching gains before merging sheets.
CAN,IMG
animated-preview-policy
Use motion only when a preview benefits the player
Images
Autoplaying video covers on every catalog card distracts keyboard users, consumes energy and may hurt initial loading.
Use static posters by default; provide a deliberate preview control and a clear stop button. Honor reduced-motion preferences for ambient animations.
Compare a 70 KB poster with a several-megabyte gameplay loop under slow mobile bandwidth to determine whether the preview improves the selection task.
Do not remove gameplay state cues when disabling decorative motion. Check pause, keyboard focus and scroll performance with ten cards.
WCAG,LCP
image-quality-acceptance
Separate verified file savings from subjective visual quality
Images
An image optimizer can accurately measure bytes without knowing whether hair, line art or tiny labels became unreadable after encoding.
Use objective format and size checks, then run human visual assessment on crops representing text, transparency and gradients. Keep those outcomes as separate claims.
If a cover shrinks from 120 KB to 62 KB, report a measured byte reduction; do not automatically call it 'better image quality'.
Encoder settings are not portable quality scores across different source art. Retain approval screenshots and review at native size before promoting a preset.
IMG,WCAG
